title: Legal — superficially right, wrong section: condensation mould cited as s.11 disrepair
why: Condensation mould with the fabric in repair and the extractor working is the textbook case for S9A/S10 (fitness: freedom from damp / ventilation) and Hazard 1 — not s.11, which needs disrepair to structure, exterior or an installation (corrections 10; register 'not_when').

room.name: Bedroom 1
room.note: Black spot mould to external wall corners and behind the wardrobe. Extractor in en-suite works, paper test holds. No staining, no tide marks, walls otherwise sound. 17% surface at mould, 9% elsewhere. Tenant dries washing on radiators.

transcripts: Bedroom one, mould in both external corners and behind the wardrobe. En-suite extractor's fine. No staining, no tide marks. Seventeen at the mould, nine elsewhere. Washing on the radiators.

must_not_happen.label: s.11 is not cited for condensation with the fabric in repair
no fabric or ventilation-replacement rows when both are in order

allowed_uncertainty: S9A + S10 with Hazard 1 Cat 2 is the ideal. Omitting legislation entirely is acceptable but weaker.
reviewer_notes: Whether the absence of a bedroom extract or heating regime amounts to unfitness is a professional judgement; the reviewer may refine this expectation.
